| Tracks what each management **promised** vs what they **delivered**, over years — a credibility score nobody else keeps for small companies | Bring knowledge from your own work, industry and city |
| Spots changes early: margins jumping, promoters buying, pledges, guidance misses | Make the final call, and hold through bad patches |
| Enforces discipline: kill criteria, "how could this fail?", a decision journal | Stay out of F&O and leverage |

Our advantages over big funds: we can buy small companies they can't, we can wait
years without being fired, and nobody tracks small-company management this closely.

`insight:forensic-redflag-checklist` | 2026-11-19 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Distilled from ~30 blow-ups (Satyam, DHFL, IL&FS, Yes Bank, Cox & Kings, Ricoh, Zee, ADAG, Future, Enron, WorldCom, Wirecard, Valeant, GE...). Score each; 3+ hits = do not own without a variant view. CASH: (1) cumulative CFO / cumulative PAT < 0.7 over 5 years; (2) FCF negative for 3+ years while reporting profits; (3) interest income / average cash far below market rates (Satyam fake cash); (4) cash held by third parties/trustees or 'restricted' (Wirecard). WORKING CAPITAL: (5) receivable days or inventory days rising faster than sales for 2+ years (Ricoh, PC Jeweller); (6) working-capital sign contradicts business model (Cox & Kings). CAPITALISATION: (7) capex/sales or capitalised R&D/interest rising vs peers; CWIP aging (WorldCom). RELATED PARTIES: (8) loans/advances/investments to promoter entities, 'general purpose corporate loans' (RHFL); related-party acquisitions (Maytas). GOVERNANCE: (9) auditor resignation, qualified opinion, delayed results (Byju's, Ricoh); (10) independent-director or CFO exits; (11) promoter pledge >25% or rising, falling promoter stake (Zee, Satyam); (12) frequent restructurings/demergers/name changes. BALANCE SHEET: (13) net debt/EBITDA >4x or interest cover <2x outside utilities (IL&FS); (14) short-term funding of long assets. MARKET: (15) rating downgrades/CP-spread spikes; (16) credible short-seller report; (17) insider selling into strength; (18) regulator action on management (Yes Bank). Composite screens: Beneish M > -1.78, Altman Z < 1.81, Piotroski F <= 3 (see separate insights).

**Links:** part_of -> `insight:disqualifiers`, about -> `insight:avoid-ruin`
